title: Importing Counterintelligence 'Tell' Catalogues Into LLM Deception Probing
original_idea: Construct probe battery based on counterintelligence tells: re-questioning, adversarial follow-ups, topic avoidance probes, cover story stress tests. Apply to models with/without planted deceptive goals.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting cross-domain transfer, but the theory that CI tells transfer to LLMs is unvalidated. The analogy between human agents hiding goals and scheming AI may not hold.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing probe batteries requires some creativity, but the implementation is prompt-based. The challenge is constructing valid CI-style probes without CI expertise. Moderate for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple probe types (re-questioning, adversarial follow-ups, topic avoidance, stress tests) across model families and sizes is moderately broad. Narrowing to 1-2 probe types would help.

novelty.reasoning: While AI is being applied to counterintelligence contexts (Tandfonline 2026 paper on AI reconfiguration of counterintelligence), and deception detection research uses interrogation-style techniques, the specific idea of importing structured counterintelligence 'tell' catalogues (re-questioning, adversarial follow-ups, topic avoidance probes, cover story stress tests) as a systematic probe battery for LLM deception is novel. Existing LLM deception probing work uses ad-hoc scenarios rather than structured forensic/CI methodologies. The cross-domain transfer from intelligence tradecraft to AI safety evaluation is creative and largely unexplored.
